PHSCS 587

Channel doping profiles

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows why rearranging the same dopant dose changes depletion electrostatics

Uniform doping is convenient, but practical channel profiles may place dopants preferentially near the surface or deeper in the body. Profile engineering balances threshold, depletion control, mobility, junction behavior and statistical variability.

For a one-dimensional depleted p-body with x measured from the surface and zero field at x = Wd, charge magnitude is |Qd| = q∫₀ᵂᵈNA(x)dx. The surface-to-bulk potential magnitude is ψs = (q/εsi)∫₀ᵂᵈxNA(x)dx. Thus the charge depends on total dose while potential also depends on its depth moment.

At fixed boundary potential, Wd is part of the solution; the displayed equal-width comparison is not a claim that two profiles have identical depletion widths under identical bias. Higher doping can strengthen electrostatic control while degrading mobility or increasing variability.

Example

For equal half-width layers, profiles [2N₀ near the surface, N₀ at depth] and [N₀, 2N₀] both integrate to 1.5N₀Wd. Their first moments are respectively 0.625N₀Wd² and 0.875N₀Wd², so their potential magnitudes differ at that imposed Wd.

Practice

1. Why does equal total dopant dose fail to ensure equal depletion potential?

Compare an integral with its depth-weighted first moment.

Dopants deeper in the depletion region contribute a larger factor x to the potential integral. Equal charge integrals can therefore have unequal potential integrals.
